sources.text: Built an interactive toy today and tested it pretty thoroughly.
Found it works smoothly—all the animations and interactions do what they're supposed to do—but when I played with it, something felt off.
The dialogue feels repetitive and thin.
It's built right, but it doesn't feel quite how I had in mind.
Decided to gather all the design ideas from the past few sessions, line them up side by side with what got built, and go through them together so I can actually say what feels wrong.

sources.text: Learned something hard about delegating: when you give three people the same instructions but tell them to make different things, they'll just make the same thing three times.
I took a shortcut on the briefs because it was faster to copy-paste one description instead of writing three completely different ones.
Cost me a lot of wasted work.
The real lesson was that shortcuts don't save time—they just move the work around.
